Jasmine / team — thanks for the ping and for the detailed redlines. I reviewed AtlasCloud_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx and have a few points and recommended snippets below. High level: we can probably agree to net-45 for this customer, but we need a firm credit policy and stronger invoicing entity language to limit exposure. Also recommend we capture VAT responsibility in an appendix (Appendix B: Tax Allocation) rather than the main body to preserve template cleanliness.

Suggested language (Order Form / Invoicing section):
1) Invoice Recipient / Payee: "Invoices will be issued by Redwood Inference, Inc. to the invoice recipient specified in the Order Form. The invoice will include the legal name and tax identification number of the Redwood entity issuing the invoice. Customer shall provide the legal name and tax identification number of the paying entity and the relevant purchase order number prior to the first invoice."

2) Payment Terms: "Unless otherwise specified in the Order Form, payment is due within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt. For AtlasCloud only, Redwood agrees to net-forty-five (45) days for invoices issued to AtlasCloud Solutions Ltd (as evidenced by PO and tax ID), subject to a one-time credit hold during onboarding not to exceed 30 days."

3) Minimum Commit True-up / Underutilization Credits: "Customer and Redwood will perform a quarterly utilization reconciliation. If actual consumption is below the committed amount for the quarter, Customer will be eligible for an underutilization credit equal to 50% of the unused committed spend for that quarter, to be applied to subsequent invoices within the next two billing cycles."

4) VAT Appendix: include a table per billing country capturing whether Redwood charges VAT, whether Customer self-reports (reverse charge), and the invoicing entity.

Operational asks for Sales/Ops: Jonas/Ben — can you confirm the exact invoicing entities we can issue (US vs EU entities) and whether accounting can append tax IDs to each invoice PDF automatically? If yes, we'll include a short acceptance criteria line in the Order Form: "Invoice meets PO requirements if legal name and tax ID match Customer-provided PO."

Once we have confirmation, I'll produce a redline response (PDF) for Maya and propose the call times.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Maya / team — thanks for the redlines and Kimberly — thanks for the clear suggested language. Quick operational confirmation from accounting/ops below and next steps to close.

1) Invoicing entities: we can issue invoices from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) and Redwood Inference Ltd (UK/EU). We can include the issuing entity legal name and tax ID on every invoice PDF. For AtlasCloud's EMEA subsidiaries we will need the exact legal name + tax ID per subsidiary (please provide in the attached CSV or PO).

2) Net terms: accounting can support net-45 specifically for AtlasCloud as a negotiated exception. We require a signed Order Form that lists the specific invoicing entity and PO reference; we will apply net-45 to invoices issued to that entity only. (This is consistent with Kimberly's proposed clause.)

3) Quarterly true-up and credits: ops can apply the underutilization credit as a line item credit on the subsequent invoice. The credit application will be automated if consumption reporting falls below the committed threshold and is agreed in the reconciliation. Ops can support the 50% credit proposal as long as it's capped at one quarter's committed spend per quarter (we'll add a cap clause).

4) Next steps / proposed call:
- I attached an operationally redlined Order Form (RF_OrderForm_v2-for-signature.docx) that incorporates Kimberly's snippets, the VAT appendix placeholder, and an invoice entity table.
- Proposed call times (30 min): Tue 21 Sep 2027 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET / 16:00 BST. Please confirm which works.
- If AtlasCloud confirms the entity list and accepts our redline language, we can push a DocuSign envelope by EOD and apply net-45 for future invoices.
